title: Qvizz: themes, round 2
question: Your two favourites, reworked for 8-word answers, plus three new ideas with a light crypto nod. Every sketch uses the same long-answer question.

options.label: Studio 72
options.lineage: 1970s TV game-show set; flip-digit boards are also the old stock-exchange boards
options.thesis: Everyone is a contestant on a 70s TV quiz; flip-digit scores give a quiet nod to the old exchange boards.
options.viewport: Question on a rounded TV-screen panel with a flip-digit timer; four wide answer podiums in a 2x2 grid, long text on two lines.
options.risk: The 70s lettering must stay on headings only, or it starts to feel like fancy dress.

options.label: Game Night
options.lineage: family board-game box: board, cards, pawns, chips
options.thesis: The big screen is a game board; players are pawns on the score track, and the vote chips double as tokens.
options.viewport: Score track with face pawns across the top; question on a wide white card; four plastic answer tiles in a 2x2 grid.
options.risk: Can lean childish if the pieces get too cute.

options.label: Trading Floor
options.lineage: exchange big boards and market tickers
options.thesis: The quiz runs like a market: players are tickers, every answer moves your price.
options.viewport: Ticker crawl of players and points across the top; question large; four full-width answer rows stacked like an order book, ideal for long answers.
options.risk: Most crypto-coded of the five; red and green read as down and up, so the answer colours move to coral, cyan, violet and gold.

options.label: The Mint
options.lineage: coin minting, medals and engraved banknote patterns
options.thesis: Points are minted coins: the timer is a gold coin, the podium hands out gold, silver and bronze.
options.viewport: A gold coin timer beside the question in a warm serif; four enamel answer plaques in a 2x2 grid on dark graphite.
options.risk: The calmest and most grown-up; needs the coin moments (reveal, podium) to bring the fun.

options.label: Block by Block
options.lineage: toy building blocks meeting a blockchain
options.thesis: Each question is a block added to the chain; the quiz literally builds a chain as you play.
options.viewport: A chain of numbered blocks across the top, the current one lit yellow; big question; four chunky answer blocks in a 2x2 grid.
options.risk: Light ground is friendlier on a TV than in a dark hall; the crypto joke is subtle and may go unnoticed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Kahoot, Mentimeter and Slido quizzes look like, done cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: White question bar, round timer, four colour blocks in a 2x2 grid.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other quiz app.
